title: Three Times as Many People Are Registering To Vote: National Voter Registration Week of Action 2026
summary: How Vote.org and its partners turned one week of action into the biggest week of 2026
body_markdown:
**How Vote.org and its partners turned one week of action into the biggest week of 2026**


This September, people across the country picked up their phones to answer this year’s most critical question to an evolving democracy: Am I registered to vote?


This National Voter Registration Week, more than **300K people turned to[Vote.org](http://vote.org/) to get vote ready** . We helped over **140K check their registration** , and helped more than **35,000 register to vote** . It was our biggest week of 2026, with nearly 2x the turnout of any other week this year.


Those numbers show the butterfly effect in action: one person takes a small step, shares it with someone they know, and inspires more people to do the same.


## The power was already in their hands


People spend hours on their phones every day. Registering to vote through Vote.org can take less than two minutes. That idea became **The Power Is in Our Hands** : an invitation to use the phone already in your hand to get ready for the midterms, then encourage someone else to do the same.


We made it easy to participate. The campaign hub offered a simple toolkit: take a photo with Vote.org on your screen, share it with a ready-made caption, and invite your community to check their registration or start registering. Shareable graphics and a live wall gave people more ways to join in and see others taking action.


## One campaign, many communities


Throughout the week, public figures, creators, artists, organizations and students brought the campaign to their audiences.


Andrew Rannells, Josh Gad, Lesley Ann Brandt, Chelsea Clinton, Piper Perabo, Monica Lewinsky, Sally Kohn and Maria Shriver encouraged their followers to check their status. Creators including @autumnbreon, @andrew.reynolds.mn and @your.richbff shared their own takes, from selfies and songs to reminders to check in with friends.


Vote.org also partnered with YelloPain to share the trailer for his film *[Simplified: Bridging the Gap](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4Xyp4fpkAhI)* , bringing a story about voting to new audiences.


Art made space for the conversation in person, too. At **The Armory Show** , Vote.org collaborated with artists **Lisu Vega, Zoë Pulley and Renee Cox** on merchandise that invited people to carry a message about civic participation beyond the fair. **Avant Arte** and **Robert Longo Studio** shared work during the week, with sales of Longo’s work supporting Vote.org.


On campuses, **Harvard Votes** and **Columbia Votes** helped bring students into the effort. Vote.org CEO **Andrea Hailey** joined student leaders from across the East Coast at the East Coast Votes Summit, hosted by the Harvard Kennedy School Institute of Politics, to speak about joy and community in civic work.


## People came ready to act


The most visited page on Vote.org that week was “ **Am I Registered to Vote?** ” It drew more than twice the traffic of our homepage. People were looking for an answer they could use.


Nearly **two out of three people using[Vote.org](http://vote.org/) were under 35.** More than **5,700 were 18 years old** , many preparing for their first election.


The response was especially strong in Texas and Iowa when measured against each state’s voting-age population. In Texas, people searched for their registration status by the thousands, and Vote.org’s Texas registration page became one of the most visited pages on the site.


Iowa also saw some of the highest engagement per eligible voter, alongside strong activity in neighboring Kansas and Nebraska.


## What comes next


More than **40 partners and public figures** participated during the week, helping the invitation travel well beyond Vote.org’s own channels. Their posts, referrals and conversations brought people to tools they could use immediately.


The work continues. Many registration deadlines happen in October, and Election Day is just around the corner. We need your help to keep the momentum going and your financial support will help us register as many voters as possible. Our tested programs have one of the lowest costs per vote in the nation so please help us today.


[Support Vote.org’s work to reach more voters before Election Day.](https://www.vote.org/donate/)


The power is in our hands. Let’s pass it on.
